c.tagline: Sri Lanka's hill-country cultural capital, home to the sacred Temple of the Tooth

taxi.fareNote: Metered tuk-tuks and the PickMe app are the norm; agree on a price beforehand for unmetered rides

emergency.note: 119 reaches police emergency services; 1990 is the Suwa Seriya free ambulance line

hood_landmark.City Center/Lake: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic

avoid.reason: Fake "helpful guide" touts around the Temple of the Tooth; tuk-tuk overcharging

hood_desc: The City Center around Kandy Lake is the heart of the city, home to the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, the Kandy National Museum, and the lakeside promenade lined with markets, restaurants, and colonial-era buildings.
Peradeniya, a few kilometers southwest, is known for its sprawling Royal Botanical Gardens and the university, giving the area a leafy, academic character with guesthouses catering to visitors.
Katukele climbs the hillside above the lake to the giant Bahirawakanda Buddha statue, offering panoramic views over the city and a quieter, more residential feel.
Getambe, further along the river toward Peradeniya, is a low-key residential and small-business area popular for mid-range guesthouses within easy reach of the botanical gardens.
Ampitiya is a hillside residential district east of the center with churches and schools, offering a calmer, local-life alternative to the tourist core.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not recommended.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-9pm; fewer trains after evening
transit.pay: Cash paid on board buses; paper tickets for trains
transit.map: No unified app; Kandy Central Bus Stand is the main hub
transit.note: Public buses and three-wheelers (tuk-tuks) are the main way to get around; the scenic railway line links Kandy to Colombo, Nuwara Eliya, and Ella

train: Scenic line to Colombo Fort (~2.5-3h) and onward to Nanu Oya/Ella through the hill country
bus: Frequent intercity and express buses connect Kandy to Colombo, Nuwara Eliya, and other cities

tip.r: Not obligatory but 10% in restaurants without a service charge, and small amounts for drivers and guides, are common and welcomed

landmarks: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa)
Sri Lanka's holiest Buddhist shrine enshrines a tooth of the Buddha within the lakeside royal palace complex, thronged by white-clad pilgrims at drumming pujas.
Kandy Lake
The scenic 1807 royal lake at the city's heart, ringed by a cloud-wall parapet, giant monitor lizards and a shaded promenade beneath the temple.
Royal Botanical Gardens, Peradeniya
Once reserved for Kandyan royalty, these 60 hectares of giant bamboo, orchid houses and a colossal Javan fig rank among Asia's finest gardens.
Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue
An 26-meter white seated Buddha gazes over the entire city from Bahirawakanda hill, glowing gold at dusk and unbeatable for panoramas.
Udawattakele Forest Reserve
A centuries-old royal forest sanctuary behind the Tooth Temple, where trails wind past hermit caves, monkeys and flashing kingfishers above the rooftops.
Kandyan Dance Performance (Kandy Cultural Centre)
Nightly shows of whirling drummers, acrobatic ves dancers and fire-walking preserve the hill capital's flamboyant courtly performance tradition.
Ceylon Tea Museum (Hantane)
A converted 1925 tea factory below Hantane peak, its vintage machinery and tastings honoring pioneers James Taylor and Thomas Lipton.
Lankatilaka, Gadaladeniya and Embekka Temples
A rewarding countryside circuit of three 14th-century Kandyan-era temples famed for rock-top settings and the finest woodcarvings in Sri Lanka.
Arthur's Seat Viewpoint
The classic lookout above the lake delivers the postcard vista of Kandy's temple rooftops, glittering water and forested hills.
Kandy Central Market
A two-story bazaar heaped with hill-country spices, jackfruit, batiks and Ceylon tea, perfect for plunging into everyday Kandyan life.

train.note: Sri Lanka is an island, so there are no international trains; Kandy railway station is a domestic hub and the gateway to the famous hill-country line onward to Hatton, Nanu Oya (for Nuwara Eliya), Ella and Badulla. Reserved seats and the 1st class observation saloon open 30 days ahead and can be bought online at Sri Lanka Railways' own site or at counters 1 and 2 in Kandy station, marked as the Intercity counter; unreserved 2nd and 3rd class tickets cannot be pre-booked and are sold at the window on the day. Important for 2026: the Colombo-Kandy-Badulla hill line was badly damaged by cyclone flooding in late 2025 and full service had still not been restored by mid-2026, so check the current running position before you plan around it. Reserved seats on the tourist stretches sell out quickly, so book as soon as the window opens.

bus.note: There are no international coaches from anywhere in Sri Lanka. Kandy's main hub is the Goods Shed bus terminal just east of the lake, with a separate Torrington stand for some Colombo and southern services; from here state-run SLTB buses (https://www.sltb.lk/) and private intercity coaches leave for Colombo (3-4 hours, or about 3 hours on the expressway services), Nuwara Eliya, Dambulla, Anuradhapura, Jaffna and the east coast. Long-distance private operators are licensed by the National Transport Commission (https://www.ntc.gov.lk/), whose site lists permitted routes and fares. Most tickets are bought at the stand on the day - only a handful of air-conditioned operators sell online, so turn up early for a seat.

ferry.note: Kandy sits inland in Sri Lanka's central highlands with no navigable water link, so there are no ferry services of any kind here; the nearest sea ports are Colombo and Trincomalee.

half.name: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
half.blurb: Rescued and orphaned elephants are bathed twice daily in the Maha Oya river at this state-run sanctuary.

half.name: Dambulla Cave Temple
half.blurb: Five cave shrines carved into a granite outcrop hold over 150 Buddha statues and ceiling murals painted across two millennia.

full.name: Sigiriya
full.blurb: A 5th-century rock fortress rises 200 meters above the plain, its base ringed by frescoes, water gardens, and mirror-polished walls.

full.name: Nuwara Eliya
full.blurb: A hill-country town built by British colonists sits amid tea plantations at over 1,800 meters elevation, cool enough for pine and eucalyptus.
